item.title: Social vulnerability amplifies global inequality in urban heat risk
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04137-z

Urban heat risk increased worldwide during 2000–2019, with growth in the Global South nearly five times that in the Global North, and conventional approaches underestimate North-South inequality by nearly 65 percent, according to an analysis of 1,029 global cities.

item.title: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04133-3

Highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glaciations; as shown using Beryllium isotopes from sediment cores from the Arctic Ocean, the Nordic Seas and the North Atlantic.

item.title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04091-w

Future climate change is projected to increase solar photovoltaic power generation in Sweden by about 5% compared to historical periods, while optimized panel tilt can boost output by 3 to 6%; according to a validated installation model incorporating air temperature, solar radiation, and snow conditions across four cities under future climate scenarios.
item.dc:title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
